specGaps: THE SUBJECT'S SHAPE (RESOLVED — pinned so no test-writer has to guess a name). src/router/metrics.hpp, namespace conductor::router, exports exactly two things. (a) `struct RequestRecord { std::string model; std::optional<std::string> role; std::optional<std::string> group; std::string priority; std::int64_t queueWaitMs{0}; std::optional<std::int64_t> upstreamMs; std::optional<std::int64_t> promptTokens; std::optional<std::int64_t> completionTokens; nlohmann::json timings; std::optional<bool> schemaMissing; std::optional<bool> schemaConformed; int status{0}; };` (b) `class MetricsLedger { explicit MetricsLedger(const RouterConfig& config); void record(const RequestRecord&); [[nodiscard]] nlohmann::json summary() const; };` — non-copyable, internally mutex-guarded. RATIONALE: this mirrors affinity.hpp's shape exactly — a dependency-light module the Router calls, with NO httplib in it. The two routes stay registered in router.hpp (where every other route lives), so the endpoints keep the pool-exhaustion property 11.4 already proved rather than acquiring a second server surface. Most rows below are therefore deterministic module-level doctests with no server at all.

QUEUE-WAIT CLOCK (RESOLVED — the draft's premise was refuted at HEAD). AdmissionController exposes no timestamps and admit() returns a bare outcome. RESOLUTION: Router::handleProxy takes std::chrono::steady_clock::now() immediately BEFORE calling admission_.admit(...) and again immediately after it returns; the difference in whole milliseconds is queueWaitMs. This is exactly right rather than merely convenient — admit() blocks the handler thread for precisely the queue wait, returns essentially instantly when a slot is free, returns instantly on Overflowed, and returns at the deadline on TimedOut — so ONE measurement covers all four outcomes and 11.4's committed, tested surface is not modified. A request that never reaches admit() (a non-POST /v1 read, which SG-6 keeps un-admitted) records queueWaitMs 0.

LEDGER JSON KEYS (APPROVED as drafted). §4.4 lines 1680-1684 name the per-line fields in prose, never as JSON keys. RESOLUTION: camelCase keys aligned with the committed TS vocabulary — model, role, group, priority, queueWaitMs, upstreamMs, promptTokens, completionTokens, timings, schemaMissing, schemaConformed, status. Every key is PRESENT on every line; absence is expressed as JSON null, never as a missing key, so a downstream reader can parse the ledger with a fixed column set.

THE `priority` COLUMN (RESOLVED — the draft was directionally right, its citation wrong). RESOLUTION: `priority` records the RESOLVED class the request was actually queued under — "interactive" | "review" | "batch" — not the raw tag. Untagged and any out-of-vocabulary tag both record "interactive", which is precisely admission.hpp priorityValue's SG-4 collapse. REASONING: the ledger is a scheduling dataset; a column that says "urgent" for a request the queue treated as interactive would make the POC's wait analysis lie. role and group have no vocabulary to collapse to, so they record the tag verbatim and null when untagged.

STREAMED USAGE EXTRACTION (APPROVED as drafted, sharpened). RESOLUTION: a NON-STREAM response parses usage/timings from the single JSON body. A STREAMED response parses them from the SSE `data:` chunk that carries a non-null `usage` object, which under Task 0.2's stream_options:{include_usage:true} arrives immediately before `data: [DONE]`; the router NEVER buffers the stream to do this — it inspects chunks as they pass and relays every byte unchanged. A response with no usage anywhere yields promptTokens/completionTokens null and changes nothing else about the request. `timings` is copied VERBATIM as a JSON value from the same object that carried usage, and is null when absent.

schemaMissing / schemaConformed AFTER THE 11.6 SHRINK (APPROVED as drafted). 11.6 shrank to the request-side schemaMissing observation because responses stream and response-validation is inert (HANDOFF, wire-notes DISCOVERY (i)). RESOLUTION: the line KEEPS both fields per §4.4's shape. schemaMissing is true/false when a request-side observation was made and null when none was (an untagged request); schemaConformed is true/false ONLY when a response-validation verdict exists and null otherwise — which under the streaming pin is all production traffic. The aggregate's schemaConformanceRate is null when zero verdicts exist. The field stays so the POC dataset's shape is stable if non-stream validation ever lands; NO validator is built in 11.7.

THE 11.6 SEAM, GIVEN 11.6 IS NOT YET WRITTEN (RESOLVED). 11.6 is NOT_STARTED in STATE.json and has no promoted spec, so 11.7 must not name its symbols. RESOLUTION: RequestRecord's schemaMissing/schemaConformed are CALLER-SUPPLIED std::optional<bool>. The metrics module performs NO schema derivation whatsoever — it never reads RequestTags.schema, never looks for response_format or grammar, and never inspects a response body for conformance. Whatever 11.6 observed is passed through to record() unmodified. That keeps every row here testable at HEAD (drive record() directly for true/false, and end-to-end for the untagged-null case) and leaves 11.6 free to shape its own surface.

ARE SHED REQUESTS LEDGERED? (APPROVED as drafted). 'One JSONL line per request' does not say whether an admission refusal gets a line. RESOLUTION: it DOES — a refused request is still a request, and the POC's wait/cost dataset needs the shed tail or the 503s are invisible. status 503, upstreamMs null, token counts null, queueWaitMs = the wait actually measured before the refusal. The same reasoning extends to the 502 upstream-unreachable envelope (row 11.7-unreachable-ledgered): the upstream WAS attempted, so upstreamMs is non-null there while the tokens are null.

WHICH REQUESTS ARE LEDGERED AT ALL (RESOLVED — the draft said '/v1' without pinning the un-admitted reads). RESOLUTION: exactly the requests that enter the committed /v1/.* proxy handler get a line — POST generation traffic, the un-admitted GET /v1/models read (SG-6), the 503 refusals and the 502 envelope alike. /conductor/health and /conductor/metrics are NEVER ledgered and never counted in the aggregate, and a path outside /v1/* never reaches the handler (httplib 404s it) so it produces no line. REASONING: 'one line per request' is read literally against the handler boundary, which is the one boundary a test can observe without reaching into the router.

WHEN THE LINE IS WRITTEN (RESOLVED — not raised by the draft, and it is the C-033 defect class). RESOLUTION: the line is appended when the RESPONSE completes, not when the handler returns. On the buffered path those coincide. On the chunked path the handler returns as soon as the content provider is registered, so the record is carried by a shared_ptr guard captured INTO the content provider exactly as AdmissionSlot already is (router.hpp line 666) — httplib destroys the provider when the response ends, normally or by the connection dying, so the line is written exactly once on every outcome. A design that records at handler return would write the streamed line before any usage chunk existed, and every token count in the production dataset would be null.

AGGREGATE FIELD NAMES AND ARITHMETIC (APPROVED as drafted, arithmetic now pinned exactly). The plan names 'count, p50/p95 wait, token totals, schema-conformance rate' while the COMMITTED consumer reads six differently-named fields. RESOLUTION: /conductor/metrics serves the UNION. MetricsSummary's exact names for the overlap — totalRequests (records recorded); schemaMissing (count of records with schemaMissing == true); schemaConformed (count with schemaConformed == true); statusCounts (object keyed by the decimal status as a string); promptTokens / completionTokens (sums over non-null values, 0 when none) — PLUS waitMsP50, waitMsP95, schemaConformanceRate. Percentiles are NEAREST-RANK over the sorted queueWaitMs samples of all recorded requests: with N > 0 samples sorted ascending and 1-indexed, waitMsP50 is the element at rank ceil(0.50*N) and waitMsP95 at rank ceil(0.95*N); with N == 0 both are 0. schemaConformanceRate = (count of schemaConformed == true) / (count of schemaConformed != null), a number in 0..1, and null when that denominator is 0. Pinned to the rank rule rather than interpolation so a doctest can assert an exact integer.

AGGREGATE SCOPE ACROSS RESTARTS (APPROVED as drafted). RESOLUTION: the endpoint serves in-memory counters accumulated since process start — O(1), no ledger re-parse, and a pre-existing ledger file contributes nothing to it. The JSONL FILE is the durable POC dataset and Phase 14's bench reads the FILE, not the endpoint. Recorded here so 14.x does not assume restart-spanning endpoint totals, and pinned by row 11.7-aggregate-in-memory.

HEALTH RESPONSE BODY (RESOLVED against committed code, superseding the draft's 'no body contract'). The route and a body already exist. RESOLUTION: 11.7 extends the SAME route's body to {"status":"ok","version":<router_version()>}; `status` keeps its committed value because src/tests/admission_test.cpp's [11.4-health-at-full-queue] asserts it, and the route stays registered outside admission so the pool-exhaustion property survives. routerHealthy needs only the 200, so nothing beyond the status code is load-bearing to the committed consumer.

LEDGER DURABILITY + PARENT DIRECTORY (APPROVED as drafted). §2.2 defaults ledgerPath to .data/router/metrics.jsonl but the plan never says who creates the directory or what the flush policy is. RESOLUTION: MetricsLedger creates the ledger's parent directory at construction if missing, opens the file APPEND-ONLY, and flushes per line — a crash loses at most the in-flight line, and a pre-existing torn final line never poisons later appends because the module only ever appends, never rewrites. HARD TEST RULE: every doctest points ledgerPath at a doctest-owned temp directory and removes it on teardown; NO test may write the §2.2 default .data/router/metrics.jsonl (the build's .data/.out untouchable rule).

FAIL-SOFT ON LEDGER I/O ERROR (APPROVED as drafted). Not named in the 11.7 bullet, but §4.4's fail-soft doctrine and G5 force it: a metrics write failure that became a 5xx would invert the fail-soft direction and make `--no-router` non-equivalent. RESOLUTION, carried as row 11.7-failsoft-ledger: a failed ledger write is logged at warn via spdlog and the proxied response is delivered unchanged, with the in-memory aggregate still updated so the endpoint does not silently under-count.

CONCURRENCY (RESOLVED — not raised by the draft). Handler threads complete concurrently by construction (maxInflightPerModel > 1, plus un-admitted reads), so two record() calls can race on one file. RESOLUTION: record() serializes the append and the counter update under one mutex owned by MetricsLedger, and each append is a single write of `<compact json>\n`. No line may be torn or interleaved with another. Pinned by row 11.7-concurrent-appends.

assertions.text: exactly ONE JSONL line is appended to config.metrics.ledgerPath per request that enters the committed /v1/.* proxy handler, and none for anything else: two sequential stub-upstream POSTs to /v1/chat/completions yield exactly two lines, each of which parses standalone as one JSON object; an un-admitted GET /v1/models yields one line; and GET /conductor/health, GET /conductor/metrics and a request to a path outside /v1/* (httplib's own 404) each append ZERO lines. Line order is response-completion order, which for the sequential case is request order

every ledger line carries §4.4's full field set (plan lines 1680-1684) under the pinned camelCase keys, with EVERY key present on EVERY line and absence expressed as JSON null rather than a missing key: model (the request body's `model`, the empty string when the body carried no usable one, matching admission's SG-3 counter key), role and group (RequestTags verbatim; null when untagged), priority (the RESOLVED class "interactive"|"review"|"batch" — an untagged request and an out-of-vocabulary tag such as "urgent" both record "interactive"), queueWaitMs, upstreamMs, promptTokens, completionTokens, timings, schemaMissing, schemaConformed, and status — status being the HTTP status actually returned to the client, so a stub upstream answering 500 records 500

queueWaitMs is the wait measured across Router::handleProxy's admit() call and nothing else — no second clock, and the committed AdmissionController is not modified: with maxInflightPerModel filled by held stub-upstream requests, a request that had to queue records a queueWaitMs at least as large as the interval it was held before release, while an immediately-admitted request records a value at or near 0, and an un-admitted GET /v1/models records exactly 0. Driven with admission_test's HoldingUpstream release gate and polls on observable state — no sleeps as the synchronization mechanism

on a NON-STREAMING upstream response (a stub that sets Content-Length) promptTokens and completionTokens come from the single JSON body's `usage` object and `timings` is copied verbatim as a JSON value from that same body; a body carrying neither records promptTokens/completionTokens/timings as null while the request still completes normally with the upstream status and bytes unchanged

on a STREAMING upstream response (a text/event-stream chunked stub, the path ALL production fan-out traffic takes per Task 0.2's stream_options:{include_usage:true}) the token counts are parsed from the SSE `data:` chunk carrying a non-null `usage` object before `data: [DONE]`, and `timings` likewise when that chunk carries it — while the stream still relays UNBUFFERED, asserted the way 11.3's [11.3-sse-incremental] asserts it: the client receives an early chunk before the stub has produced the last one. A streamed response with no usage chunk records null token counts and still relays every byte

a streamed request produces EXACTLY ONE ledger line and that line is appended after the stream COMPLETES, not when the handler returns: while the chunked stub is still producing, the ledger file holds zero lines for that request; after `data: [DONE]` has crossed and the client's response has ended, it holds exactly one, carrying the token counts from the usage chunk. A downstream disconnect mid-stream still yields exactly one line, never zero and never two — the record guard is captured by the content provider exactly as AdmissionSlot already is (the C-033 defect class, which the always-Content-Length stubs would otherwise hide)

the schema fields are recorded verbatim from what the caller supplies and metrics derives NOTHING itself — it never reads RequestTags.schema, never looks for response_format or grammar, and never inspects a response body: recording a RequestRecord with schemaMissing true, false and nullopt writes JSON true, false and null respectively, and the same three cases hold for schemaConformed; end-to-end, an UNTAGGED request through the real Router records schemaMissing null and schemaConformed null (no observation and no verdict were made), and under the streaming pin every streamed response records schemaConformed null

an admission-refused request still gets its ledger line, so the shed tail is visible in the POC dataset: a queue-overflow 503 records status 503, upstreamMs null, promptTokens/completionTokens null and a queueWaitMs at or near 0 (Overflowed returns immediately, never after a wait), while a queue-timeout 503 records status 503, upstreamMs null, null token counts and a queueWaitMs of at least admission.queueTimeoutMs — and in both cases the upstream stub saw NO request for that marker

the router-origin 502 envelope is ledgered too: with no upstream listening on the configured port, the proxied request answers 502 with 11.3's sendRouterError envelope AND appends exactly one line recording status 502, null promptTokens/completionTokens, and a NON-null upstreamMs (the upstream was attempted, unlike a shed request) — the ledger never silently drops a router-origin status, or the aggregate's statusCounts would understate every failure the fan-out side sees

GET /conductor/metrics answers 200 with the pinned union aggregate over a known request mix driven through the stub: totalRequests equals the number of recorded requests; schemaMissing and schemaConformed are the COUNTS of records whose respective field is true; statusCounts is an object keyed by the decimal status as a string (e.g. {"200":3,"503":1}); promptTokens and completionTokens are sums over non-null values (0 when none); waitMsP50 and waitMsP95 are the nearest-rank percentiles of the sorted queueWaitMs samples at 1-indexed ranks ceil(0.50*N) and ceil(0.95*N), asserted as EXACT values for a hand-computed sample set and both 0 when N is 0; and schemaConformanceRate is (schemaConformed-true) / (schemaConformed non-null), null when that denominator is 0. The six overlapping names are byte-identical to the COMMITTED conductor/adapter/router-client.ts MetricsSummary, which casts without validating

GET /conductor/metrics is registered OUTSIDE admission, exactly as GET /conductor/health already is, and answers 200 with a parseable body while every in-flight slot is held and the queue is full — the same pool-exhaustion proof as 11.4's [11.4-health-at-full-queue], run against the metrics route. Serving it neither appends a ledger line nor increments totalRequests, so polling the endpoint can never inflate the dataset it reports

GET /conductor/health answers HTTP 200 — the exact contract the committed routerHealthy requires — with the EXTENDED body {"status":"ok","version":<conductor::router::router_version()>}: `status` still equals "ok" (11.4's committed [11.4-health-at-full-queue] asserts it and must stay green), `version` equals router_version() rather than a second version constant, and the route answers while proxied traffic is in flight. The full-queue variant remains 11.4's assertion and is not duplicated here

the ledger location comes ONLY from the already-parsed RouterConfig::metrics.ledgerPath (§2.2 plan line 666; required in the exported RouterConfig.schema.json): a config pointing at a doctest-owned temp path writes exactly there and nowhere else, the parent directory is CREATED when missing, two MetricsLedger instances built from configs naming different paths write to their own files only, the path is never hardcoded, and no test writes the §2.2 default .data/router/metrics.jsonl

a ledger write failure NEVER fails the proxied request (G5: the router must never fail a request the direct path would have served): with ledgerPath pointing into a location that cannot be written, the client still receives the upstream response with the SAME status, headers and body bytes as the healthy-ledger case, the failure is logged at warn via spdlog (captured with a test sink), the router mints no 5xx of its own, and GET /conductor/metrics still answers 200 with the in-memory aggregate counting that request

concurrent completions never tear or interleave a line: with N concurrent requests completing against the stub, the ledger file holds exactly N lines, EVERY line parses standalone as a JSON object carrying the full pinned key set, the set of per-request markers recovered from those lines equals the set sent, and the aggregate's totalRequests equals N — the append and the counter update are serialized under one mutex owned by MetricsLedger

the aggregate is in-memory since process start and is NEVER a re-read of the ledger file: constructing a MetricsLedger over a ledgerPath whose file ALREADY contains well-formed lines from a prior run yields totalRequests 0 and zeroed counters before anything is recorded, and after recording K requests it reports exactly K — the pre-existing lines are preserved on disk (the module appends, never rewrites or truncates) but contribute nothing to the endpoint, which is why Phase 14's bench must read the FILE rather than the endpoint
